granularity.containers: <file>::impl X | impl T for X | mod m | struct S | enum E | trait T

ground_truth_rules: member addition is attributed to the enclosing container and the file, never to a synthetic function
import and top-level static/const edits are file-level only
comment-only and doc-comment-only hunks are ignored
commits whose gold patch is entirely file creation or deletion are excluded; created/deleted files inside a mixed commit are dropped from the gold set
commits with any gold file absent from HEAD are excluded
class_rule: verbatim iff the query contains, as a whole word, a gold file basename stem or a gold container/function identifier (len>=4, excluding 'mod'/'tests'); otherwise descriptive
head_state_deviation: The runner scores against the daemon index of the current HEAD, not the paper's pre-PR snapshot. Gold locations therefore refer to symbols as they exist after the fix landed.
manual_verification: every entry below was checked against `git show <sha>` by hand; per-entry adjudication in `notes`

queries.query:
fix(presets): remove refresh_symbol_index from MINIMAL_TOOLS (dogfood patch)

Daemon redeploy of the b07d5773 binary surfaced a real violation
from find_over_visible_apis:

  refresh_symbol_index has annotations="mut_w"
  (audit_category="mutation", approval_required=true)
  but was listed in MINIMAL_TOOLS

The Minimal preset is the surface a planner agent uses when it should
not be able to initiate mutations — the leak meant a Minimal-bound
caller could trigger an index rebuild without surfacing the
approval-required intent. find_over_visible_apis flagged it as a
single concrete violation (violation_count=1, surface=preset:minimal).

Patch:
  - presets.rs::MINIMAL_TOOLS — removed refresh_symbol_index (line 167)
    with an inline comment explaining the dogfood finding so the next
    reader has the audit-trail without having to grep.
  - tools.toml — refresh_symbol_index.preset_tags goes from
    ["minimal", "builder-minimal"] to ["builder-minimal"] only.
  - build_generated.rs regenerated via scripts/regen-tool-defs.py.

The tool remains in BUILDER_MINIMAL_TOOLS (where build-agent mutation
is expected) and the broader Full preset (where set_preset full
explicitly opens the mutation surface). Callers that need it from a
minimal-bound session must set_preset full first — surfacing the
intent rather than hiding it.

Re-running find_over_visible_apis against the patched binary will
report violation_count=0. This is the first real defect surfaced by
the Self-auditability detector family that was built up in Sprint 2.
Proof that the cycle is doing the job it was built for.

cargo check + clippy --features http,semantic + fmt + 14
surface_audit_tests + regen-tool-defs.py --check all pass.

queries.query:
fix(artifact_store): require tool_name match in L3 cold tier (#G2)

L3 cold-tier fallback previously matched on scope + generic
cache_key alone, allowing a stored `dead_code_report` artifact to
be returned verbatim for an unrelated `module_boundary_report`
call when the latter's `cache_key` happened to miss L1/L2. The two
tools produce structurally different payloads (summary, findings,
section layout), so the fallback was payload-poisoning rather than
useful reuse.

Add `tool_name == tool_name` to the L3 predicate so all three tiers
require tool match. L3's purpose now is "same tool + same scope +
generic artifact" with surface relaxed (so e.g. planner-readonly
can reuse a refactor-full artifact). Replace the cross-tool hit
test with an isolation regression test and add an L3 same-tool
different-surface hit test.

Discovered via self-dogfood (2026-05-18).

queries.query:
fix(dead_code_report): accept `path` as soft alias of `scope` (#G1)

`dead_code_report` is the only composite report tool that argues
over `scope`; the rest of the family (`impact_report`,
`module_boundary_report`, `refactor_safety_report`,
`diff_aware_references`, …) takes `path`. The dispatch envelope's
`apply_path_alias_normalisation` normalises
`file_path`/`path`/`relative_path` for handlers that opt in, but
`scope` is not part of that contract. A caller copy-pasting the
sibling-tool convention sent `{"path":"crates/..."}` and the
handler silently fell back to `scope = "."`, scanning the project
root and surfacing false positives like `.cargo/audit.toml`.

Accept `path` as a soft alias in both the sync (`boundary.rs`) and
async-job (`report_jobs.rs`) handlers, include `path` in the cache
key so path-only callers still benefit from L1/L2 reuse, and add
`path` to the tools.toml input schema with a description marking
it as the alias. Re-run `scripts/regen-tool-defs.py --write` to
sync the generated registry.

Bonus: with the narrower scope honored, the legacy false positives
from `.cargo/audit.toml` etc. drop out of `top_findings` naturally.

Discovered via self-dogfood (2026-05-18).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
queries.notes: three free fns across three files; build_generated.rs is codegen output but is a genuine gold file for this patch.

queries.query:
fix(test): make prepare_harness stale-daemon fixture deterministic (filetime) (#335)

* fix(test): make prepare_harness stale-daemon fixture deterministic

`prepare_harness_session_warns_when_daemon_binary_is_stale` had been
flaking single-shot across our recent sweep (PR-K #328, #312, #334 each
saw it fail exactly once on ubuntu while the rest of the matrix was
green). Two earlier remediations (PRs #174/#177/#184/#185/#187/#292) had
landed:

  1. `TEST_ENV_LOCK` — serialises tests touching
     `CODELENS_EXECUTABLE_PATH_OVERRIDE`.
  2. A 1.5 s `thread::sleep` — tried to advance wall-clock past
     `daemon_started_at`'s second boundary before writing the override
     file so its `mtime` would land in a later RFC3339 second.

Layer 2 still depended on `SystemTime::now()` actually advancing through
a full second during the sleep, which under contended CI scheduling is
not bounded by the requested duration. Same shape of bug as #332's
`subsec_nanos`-only path collisions: the fixture relied on a wall-clock
side-effect instead of a deterministic assignment.

Fix: replace the sleep with an explicit
`filetime::set_file_mtime(override_path, daemon_started_at + 10s)`. The
`mtime > daemon_started_seconds` relationship is now a property of the
assignment, independent of the runner's scheduler. The 10 s headroom
comfortably clears any plausible second-boundary issue without
depending on wall-clock advancement.

`filetime = "0.2"` is already a dev-dep; the rest of the test tree
already uses this exact pattern (`scip_health`, `metrics_config::capabilities`).

Validation:
- 10 consecutive local runs — all PASS in 0.05-0.11 s (vs 1.68 s
  before; sleep removal saves ~1.5 s per run too).
- `cargo test -p codelens-mcp --bin codelens-mcp` — 593 passed / 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --features http,semantic -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --no-default-features -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

No production code touched. `build_info::daemon_binary_drift_payload`
already enforces the second-precision contract correctly; the existing
`build_info::tests::classify_drift_*` suite covers the boolean
combinations. This is a fixture-side fix only.

queries.query:
fix(audit): set busy_timeout on audit_log connections

The instrumented preflight asserts (7f048dd8) surfaced the real CI
failure: mutations were rejected with "mutation audit sink unavailable
... failed to migrate audit_log schema" before ever reaching the
preflight gate. AuditSink::open had no busy_timeout (default 0ms), so
any concurrent opener of the same audit_log.sqlite fails schema
init/migration with an immediate SQLITE_BUSY. Production shares one
project audit dir across four daemons, so this was a live mutation-path
hazard, not just test flake. Match the symbol-index 30s policy.

fix(clippy): satisfy manual_filter lint on Rust 1.97 (unblock CI) (#381)

CI's stable toolchain rolled to 1.97, whose clippy::manual_filter lint flags
configured_rerank_blend's range clamp `.and_then(|v| if (0.0..=1.0).contains(&v)
{ Some(v) } else { None })`. `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` fails on
it across all five CI feature variants (default/http/otel/scip-backend/
no-default), blocking every PR's `test` job — not any code change.

Rewrite to the equivalent `.filter(|v| (0.0..=1.0).contains(v))`. Behavior
identical: keep the parsed CODELENS_RERANK_BLEND only when in [0.0, 1.0], else
fall back to 0.75.

Verified with clippy 0.1.97 locally: all five variants clean under -D warnings,
cargo check OK.

queries.query:
fix(jobs): give each durable job write a unique staging file

update()/store()/cancel()/recover paths write the same job record with
no lock held; the fixed <id>.json.tmp staging name let one writer rename
the other's staging file away, failing the loser with ENOENT — the
refresh_symbol_index_background_queues_and_completes_job flake under
parallel test load. Staging names now carry pid + a process-wide nonce
so the final rename stays an atomic last-writer-wins, and a failed
rename cleans up its own staging file. Pinned by a 4-thread hammer test
that reproduced the race deterministically on the old code.

queries.query:
fix(tests): stop deleting the entire system temp dir in delegate test

The delegate-telemetry test placed its jsonl directly in
std::env::temp_dir() and cleaned up with remove_dir_all(parent) — the
parent IS the system temp dir, so every run deleted every concurrent
test's fixture tree. This is the dominant root cause behind the
rotating CI-macOS failures this cycle chased: symbols.db vanishing
mid-write ("database is locked"), staged principals.toml vanishing
before discovery (RBAC ReadOnly denials on a Refactor fixture), audit
dirs vanishing ("mutation audit sink unavailable"), and background-job
fixtures vanishing mid-refresh (IO ENOENT). The earlier busy_timeout
and fixture-uniqueness fixes remain valid hardening, but this line was
the assassin. Delete only the test's own file.

writer_tests.rs remove_dir_all(parent) calls are safe — their paths
live inside per-test subdirectories, audited this commit.
